summary.short: Sets security requirements for internet- and network-connectable consumer products sold in the UK, with duties for manufacturers, importers and distributors enforced by the Secretary of State. Part 2 amends electronic communications infrastructure rules. Most provisions commence by regulations.
summary.long: The Act sets security requirements for internet-connectable and network-connectable consumer products made available in the UK (Part 1). The Secretary of State may specify requirements by regulations, and manufacturers, importers and distributors must comply with them, provide a statement of compliance before supply, investigate and remedy compliance failures, notify the enforcement authority and customers, and keep records for 10 years. Importers and distributors may not supply products known to have a compliance failure, and non-UK manufacturers may appoint UK authorised representatives. Enforcement uses compliance, stop and recall notices, forfeiture orders, and monetary penalty notices up to the greater of £10 million or 4% of qualifying worldwide revenue; failing to comply with an enforcement notice is an offence. Part 2 amends the electronic communications code on infrastructure sharing, upgrades, code rights for unresponsive occupiers, alternative dispute resolution and compensation, and tenancy rent rules in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, and gives the Secretary of State regulation-making powers for network access rights. Most provisions commence by regulations.

notes: Commencement: s.27 and ss.76-80 came into force on the day of passing; other provisions commence by regulations under s.79(2). The text contains no commencement regulations, so the registry status in_force is not confirmed by the text. Part 4ZA, and the Schedule amendments tied to it, depend on s.67 coming fully into force. Penalty maxima are stated in s.36(5) (daily penalty not exceeding £20,000) and s.38(1) (greater of £10 million and 4% of qualifying worldwide revenue). Obligations in Chapter 2 are framed by reference to security requirements that are not set in this text (s.1). Enforcement under Chapter 3 applies only to Part 1 (s.26). Extent is UK-wide (s.78), with separate Scottish and Northern Irish procedures. No internal inconsistency was identified.
